title: Tail and focus a pane that no bead claims
description:
Graeme, on the live screen: *we should be able to view panes that fall into the no project/unattributed categories.*

An unattributed or unconfigured pane is a live agent doing work. `bdi` already draws its line — `draw.rs:214-215` gives both `Item::Loose` and `Item::Unconfigured` a `loose_line` carrying the pane id, its status and its cwd — so you can see that it exists. You cannot look at it.

**`target()` refuses every line that is not a bead.** `tail.rs:174-186` returns `Target::NotABead` unless `line.content` is `Content::Bead(_)`, then finds the pane by walking from the bead's key to its `AgentRef`. A loose pane's line has no `Line::bead`, so the tail says *select a bead to see what is on it* and `⏎` focuses nothing — on a row that names a pane in its own text.

So the one case where `bdi` knows a pane exists and refuses to show you what is on it is the case where the pane is not yet joined to any bead. That is the case Graeme is in right now with a second project running, and it is the opposite of what the tool is for: **no live agent is hidden**, which `bdi-xey` states as the principle behind the fold defaults, should hold for the tail as well as for the forest.

**The rule to implement: a line that names a pane can be tailed and can be focused.** Three kinds of line name one and none of them can be today:

- `Item::Loose` — a pane in a configured project no bead claims.
- `Item::Unconfigured` — a pane in a directory no configured project covers.
- `Item::Conflict` — but only where the arm names exactly one pane. `PaneInAnotherProject` and `SeveralBeadsNameOnePane` do; `BeadAndPaneDisagree` names two and `SeveralPanesNameOneBead` names several, so both stay `NotABead` because there is genuinely nothing to pick.

**The rule, which sorts a future arm without a list to maintain: a row can be tailed exactly when it names one pane.**

`Content::Item` carries the whole `Item`, so every pane is reachable from an item line without going through a bead and without a lookup. That is `Target`'s shape, not the forest's: the tail gets to a pane along one road today, from a bead key through the snapshot's trees, and it needs a second road for a pane that arrives already named.

**The selection cannot reach an item line, and that half is not this bead.** `selectable` (`forest.rs:767`) matches `Tree | Bead | Elided | Group` and omits `Content::Item`, and both `scan` and `step` filter through it, so no motion returns an item row. `handle_at` (`:414`) falls through to `line.bead`, which `draw_groups` (`:741`) sets to `None` on every item, so an item has no `Handle` and `settle_cursor` (`:441`) would put the selection back on the first tree at the next refresh. Making the tail answer for an item therefore changes nothing on screen on its own. That work is `bdi-2bb.19`, in `forest.rs`, and this bead is blocked behind it.

**What must not change.** `Target::NoAgent` and `Target::NotABead` still exist and still mean what they meant — a bead nobody is working, and a header, group or note. A group's own line names no pane and must keep saying so. `moved_on` is defined over `target(forest).pane()` and should keep working unchanged once `target` can answer for these lines; the test `two_beads_on_one_pane_do_not_read_it_twice` is the guard that says the tail is not re-read on every move, and it must stay green.

**Done when** selecting an unattributed pane, an unconfigured pane or a conflicted pane shows that pane's rows in the tail, `⏎` focuses it, the phrase for a row that genuinely names no pane is unchanged, and `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `nix flake check` are green with CI green on the pushed commit.

**Files owned.** `src/view/tail.rs`, and `src/view/phrase.rs` only if a phrase must change.
notes:
Filed off Graeme's live screen at 18:06 BST on 2026-08-30, while a second project of his was running with no [[projects]] entry covering it. The panes he could not look at were that project's.
The selection cannot land on an item line, so widening target() alone changes nothing on screen. forest.rs:767-772 selectable() omits Content::Item, and scan()/step() filter through it; forest.rs:414-420 handle_at() gives an item no Handle (draw_groups builds every item line with bead: None), so a selectable item would lose the cursor and settle_cursor would bounce the selection back to the first tree on the next refresh. Measured with a throwaway test: forty NextRow presses over a snapshot with one unattributed pane leave the selection on the group line above it. That is bdi-2bb.19, on the seat that owns forest.rs, and this bead is wired behind it.
Resume state. The tail half is written and pushed to the branch and commit in metadata (wip_branch, wip_commit), off b9c664f. Not delivery. 20 tests green, 6 red, and all six are red at the same step_onto assertion because the selection cannot reach a group's item line. Green and load-bearing: two_beads_on_one_pane_do_not_read_it_twice, and a pairwise moved_on guard over a forest carrying loose panes and conflicts. Red until bdi-2bb.19 lands: the four pane-bearing kinds tailed and focused, the two ambiguous conflicts and a failed project still silent, no-herdr still winning on a loose row, and the selection holding the same pane across a refresh that reorders its group. To resume: rebase the branch onto main, run cargo test. The six going green with no change to src/view/tail.rs is the test of whether the tail half is right; needing to edit that file is a finding about the forest's shape and goes to beady-eye/v1-bdi-2bb.18, not absorbed as a fix. Then clippy, fmt on tail.rs only, nix flake check on the committed tree, squash against $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main), push to main, delete the branch, close on the CI run id.

title: The pane worker does I/O from inside the view layer
description:
`docs/design.md` says the collector is *"the only unit that does I/O"*.
`src/view/tail.rs` spawns a thread that shells out to `herdr`.

105 lines of subprocess orchestration living in `view/`: `Panes` (:31), `Job`
(:39), `Done` (:46), `Herdr` (:57 — owns a `Runner`, `mpsc` channels, a
`Cell<usize>` of outstanding requests), the `PATIENCE` timeout protocol
(:63-90), `no_answer` (:96), `work` (:105) calling `herdr::agent_read` and
`herdr::agent_focus`, and the impl (:117-136). `src/tui.rs:33` constructs it
as `Herdr::new(RealRunner)`.

The rest of the file — `Tail` (:144), `Target` (:151), `target` (:174), `agent`
(:189), `tail` (:205), `moved_on` (:232), `focus` (:245) — is pure decision
logic over a `Forest` and a `&dyn Panes`, and is the only part `view/` should
own.

**Move `Panes`, `Job`, `Done`, `Herdr`, `PATIENCE`, `no_answer` and `work` into
a new `src/collect/panes.rs`.** `tail.rs` imports `collect::panes::Panes`;
`tui.rs` imports `Herdr` from there. The seam already exists — `Panes` is the
trait — so this is a move, not a redesign.

## Done when

- Nothing under `src/view/` constructs a `Runner` or names a subprocess.
- `tail.rs` holds only decision logic over `Forest` and `&dyn Panes`.
- The `PATIENCE` timeout behaviour is unchanged and still has its test.

title: Bring docs/design.md in line with the TUI that got built
description:
`docs/design.md` was the starting point, not gospel. The TUI section is thirty
lines and one worked screen, and the screen disagrees with the prose in several
places; every one of those is settled by the seat that hits it, at the point it
hits it, with the code in front of it. This bead runs **last** and brings the
document into line with what actually got built.

**Do not treat this as a gate.** Nothing waits on it. It exists so the spec
does not quietly rot into a description of a program nobody wrote.

**What it reconciles, and where each was decided:**

| Decided in | What |
|---|---|
| `bdi-2bb.3` | the status glyphs `●○◐◍`, which appear in the mock and in no terminology table; and the id-abbreviation rule (`.20` for `nix-9670s.20`), including what it does for a node whose id does not share its root's prefix |
| `bdi-2bb.4` | the elision rule — line 354 says *"closed subtrees collapse to a count"* while the mock's `… 13 more` reads as *"the remaining 13 nodes"*; the fold rule, where line 489 (roots collapsed by default, expanded on the selected one) fights line 513 (`space` folds); and where `dangling`, `unreachable`, `truncated`, `conflicts` and `failed_projects` appear, since the sketch shows none of the five |
| `bdi-2bb.6` | the refresh interval, which line 515 leaves as *"a default interval"* |
| `bdi-2bb.7` | what `⏎` does on a row with no pane — most rows have none, and the mock never shows that state |
| `bdi-2bb.8` | the notification protocol and its socket, which that bead writes into `README.md` — lift it, don't re-derive it |

**Also fix, while in there:** the JSON example (~lines 451–484) shows
`"anomaly": null` where the shipped model emits `anomalies: []`. The prose
already governs and the code already follows it — this is drift in the sample.

**And the loose-pane contract, decided in `bdi-1pn` and landed in `168702b`.**
A pane resolving to no bead is now reported as one of two things, and the
document still describes one:

- The `unattributed` entry in the JSON sample (:484) needs its `project` field
  — that field is now always present on an `unattributed` entry, never absent.
- The sample needs a second top-level array beside it, `unconfigured`, holding
  the panes whose directory sits under no `[[projects]]` entry. Its entries are
  `{"pane", "cwd", "pane_status"}` and carry no `project` key at all; that
  absence is the contract, so a consumer tests for the key rather than reading
  a null.
- The findings table (:333) needs a row for `unconfigured` beside the
  `unattributed` one, and the sentence at :307 — "a pane belonging to no
  configured project joins nothing and lands in `unattributed`" — is now wrong
  and should say `unconfigured`.
- The worked screen (:515) shows one group; there are two, and the new one
  draws above `unattributed`, where the projects with nothing to show are.
- The terminology table already has the `unconfigured` row; `bdi-1pn` added it.

**And the agent cell, decided in `bdi-qv1` and landed in `7c11fba`.** The cell
drew the pane id. herdr displays a pane id nowhere in its own UI — only in its
socket API and its JSON — so a reader had no way to turn one into a pane they
could look at. It now draws what the pane says it is doing:

    ◍ <caption, else pane id> · <state> · <join caveat, where inferred>

- The caption is `Pane::caption()`, already carried to the row on
  `AgentRef.title`: the state label for the state the pane is in, falling back
  to the pane title. Not `display_agent`, which seats set to their own bead id
  and which would repeat the row two columns to its left.
- A pane carrying neither label nor title keeps its id. There it is not noise —
  it is the only thing left telling one live agent from another.
- The separator is the row's own `·`. A pane id was a token and parsed on
  sight; a caption is free text and `waiting at a prompt` is three words, so
  run together they read as one sentence. The state stays between the caption
  and the join caveat: the caveat says how we know which pane this is, not what
  the pane is doing, and against the caption it would read as doubt about the
  work.
- The pane id is demoted, not gone. It still names the tail's own rule, where a
  reader has already chosen one pane, and every `Conflict` carries it in its own
  fields — so nothing that reports a disagreement lost the ability to say which
  pane it means.
- The worked screen (:515) shows pane ids in the agent column; those become
  captions.

**And correct the standing instruction.** `CLAUDE.md` says *"docs/design.md is
the spec. It is accepted; changes to it are design decisions, not edits."*
Graeme superseded that on 2026-08-30: the design is a starting point and we
deviate as we learn. Left standing, that line tells every future seat the
opposite of the rule it is working under.

**And the foot of the screen, decided in **bdi-2bb.13** and landed in
**09ea782**.** The document has no account of the status bar at all, and there
is now a rule to record along with what it draws.

- **Terminology, coined:** **notice** — something true of the view as a whole
  rather than of any row in it, said at the foot of the screen. The
  terminology table needs the row; `notice` was free as of `168702b`.
- **The rule that decides what goes there: the foot is for facts that have no
  row to sit on.** Two qualify today. A herdr that could not be reached empties
  the agent column on every row. A `bdi` whose inbound socket would not open is
  told nothing when a project changes, so the whole view is only as fresh as the
  refresh interval. Neither has a row that is wrong, which is why neither can be
  said anywhere else.
- **The rule's other edge: a per-project fact never belongs there.** It has a
  tree, and its header is where the reader is already looking at the thing it is
  about — a tracker that refused a credential is drawn on its own tree, not in
  the foot. The foot is one line, so a per-project fact there is a fact that
  evicts other facts.
- **The order is by consequence, and the foot gives up the last first.** The
  keys yield before any notice, because a key can be rediscovered and a fact
  silently absent from the one row nothing can fold or scroll away is a fact the
  reader never learns.
- **The socket failure is said twice, deliberately, and the two are not
  copies.** The notice says what it costs the reader — the view is polled
  rather than reported. The `stderr` line names the path and the `io::Error`
  under it, which is the actionable half (another `bdi` holding the socket is
  closed by hand) and precisely the half `phrase.rs` forbids on screen. It is
  written before the alternate screen opens, so it survives the teardown, and it
  can be redirected to a file where a status bar never can. The notification
  protocol section (`bdi-2bb.8`'s row above) should say so, or a future reader
  seeing an `eprintln!` beside a status-bar notice will reasonably delete one.

**A finished branch draws as one line and rests shut.** A branch is finished
when every bead in it is closed, with no agent and no anomaly anywhere beneath
it — the whole branch, not merely its head. Its glyph, its fraction and its fold
marker already say *finished, and holds more*; opening it is the ordinary fold.
A run of such branches is drawn as a count where there are enough of them, and
because its members are finished branches its phrase is true of every bead it
counts, not merely of the siblings it names. A closed branch is drawn open, in
spite of all this, when a live agent or an anomaly sits anywhere inside it.

**Done when** `docs/design.md` describes the TUI that exists — no rule left
undefined that the code decided, no sample contradicting the model — and
`CLAUDE.md` states the design's real standing.

**Out of scope.** Deciding any of the above. Each is the decision of the bead
that owns it; this bead only records what they chose.

**Files owned.** `docs/design.md`, `CLAUDE.md`.
notes:
Four things the TUI now does that `docs/design.md` still contradicts, each settled by a landed bead. Recorded here because the seats that decided them are gone.

**The keys row lost `^R` (`bdi-2bb.12`, `8b227ab`).** Naming keys in words cost columns: the row went 37 → 53, and at forty columns `Fitted` cuts from the right, so `q quit` vanished. Refresh is the most skippable of the five — `bdi` collects on a timer and on change reports anyway, so `^R` only ever means *now* — and `?` is one key from the full list. The row is back to 37 columns: `Enter focus   a all   ? keys   q quit`. `docs/design.md` shows the old row at line 517 and the old bindings at 520.

**The bindings table is ordered least-guessable first, not naturally.** Ordered naturally, the eight-row case gave a reader six motion keys and '8 more' — the arrows, which they would have pressed anyway. Ordered this way they get Enter, Space, `a`, `?`, `q`, `^R` and a count. A reader who cannot see the arrows presses one regardless; one who cannot see `a` never works out that the trees they are missing are being filtered. Pinned character-for-character in `eight_rows_hold_the_way_out_the_keys_worth_most_and_a_count_of_the_rest`.

**Control-held-down moves a row, and always has.** The old match had `KeyCode::Char('j') | KeyCode::Down` with no modifier guard; only `d`, `u`, `r` and `c` ever asked for control. `bdi-2bb.12` reproduced it exactly rather than changing it, and named the field so control reads as a requirement rather than an exclusion. It is now visible where it was not, and a reader will take it for a decision. It is not one. If it should change, that is its own bead.

**An opened elided run re-elides inside itself (`bdi-2bb.11`).** The two-or-more quiet-closed rule is a property of the forest, not of a place in it, so `… 7 more` opens to reveal closed siblings that may themselves show a nested `… 3 more`. Revealed beads hang *under* the run line rather than splicing into the parent's sequence, which keeps the box-drawing well-formed and makes `h`/`l` step in and out of the run through the existing depth arithmetic. The counts still reconcile exactly because `subtree_size` is recursive. Drawing flat instead means `space` on `… 143 more` dumps 143 lines you can only fold back by shutting the whole run.
Two rules from the `bdi-2bb.11` seat, in the words it settled them in. Both are `docs/design.md`'s to record.

**An open run re-elides inside itself.** The two-or-more quiet-closed rule is a property of the forest, not of a place in it, so it applies inside an open run exactly as it does everywhere else. The account still reconciles, because the count is recursive: open `… 7 more` and you get the closed siblings, and where a sibling's own children are a quiet run of two or more, a nested `… 3 more`. Nothing disappears; it is counted one level down.

**An opened run's beads hang under the run line, not beside the siblings they belong to.** A run is always the last of its parent's entries, so a sibling drawn after it at that depth would follow an elbow that had already said it was the last. Nesting keeps the box-drawing well-formed and means `h` and `l` step out of and into the run through the depth arithmetic that was already there.

**And the marker convention, which the bead's own sketch had wrong.** The fold marker goes in the prefix, not in `draw.rs`'s `Content::Elided` arm — that is where every other fold in the file puts it, and `marker()`'s doc states the convention: a shut node says so; an open node says it by drawing its children. So a shut run draws `└── ▸ … 2 more` and an open one draws `└── … 2 more` with its beads beneath, exactly as a bead does. A marker in the arm would have been the one fold in the forest that announced itself twice.
**The invariant `docs/design.md` is missing, and should state once rather than three times: no live agent is hidden — not by a fold, not by an elision, not by a filter.**

Three beads are each one place `bdi` currently breaks it, by a different mechanism:

- `bdi-4av` — an elided run's phrase denies a live agent its own count includes.
- `bdi-mse` — quiet is tested on a member and applied to its whole subtree, so a run drags live work behind it. Supersedes `bdi-4av`.
- `bdi-xey` — the default fold state hides agents nobody has navigated to. Graeme: *by default we should expand any beads necessary to show all workers.*

The model already reasons this way in the other direction — the live-agent filter collapses a tree with **no** live agent into `hidden_trees` — so the invariant is the dual of a rule the design has had since v1, never written down as a rule. Writing it down is what makes the next feature that would break it obvious before it ships rather than after Graeme reads a screen.

Also for the design: the default is *not* full expansion and *not* collapsed-except-selected. It is the spine to each agent open and everything else shut, so the first screen answers who is working on what.
**Two layout rules from the `bdi-7y9` seat, in its own words, both needing `docs/design.md`.**

**Where the header's status glyph goes: between the fold marker and the tree.** `▾ ● summit-works · nix-9670s  lift the ground station    0/3`. Every other line reads box-drawing, then glyph, then who it is. The fold marker *is* the header's box-drawing — same column, and it says the same kind of thing, how the tree is shaped rather than how it is going. Putting the glyph after it gives one reading order down the whole screen; putting it first would make the header the only line that inverts that order, to save nothing.

**When a line carries a closed/total count: a line that stands for more than itself says how much of that is done.** So a leaf gets a glyph and no count; a node with children gets a glyph and closed/total over its own subtree including itself; a root gets the same, which stops the root being a special case at all.

Keyed on **structure**, not on `issue_type == \"epic\"`. Reading a display rule out of bd's taxonomy is interpreting what a field means, which this project's rules push into config. *Has children* needs no interpretation — it is the shape of the tree `bdi` already computes, and it is exactly the condition under which the question is askable. The count includes the line's own bead, because that is what a root already does: `snapshot.rs` sets `total: nodes.len()` and `nodes` includes the root, so it is one rule at every depth.

Why it earns its width: a shut node hides its children completely, and the count is what makes shutting it safe — which is the root's own reason for having one.

An unreachable tracker reports no root, so its header draws no glyph and says why it failed instead, rather than inventing a status bd never gave.
**Three more, from the glyph column (bdi-7y9, landed).** docs/design.md's
worked screen shows a header with no status glyph and nested lines with no
count, and both are now wrong.

**A tree header carries its root's own status, after the fold marker:
`▾ ● summit-works · nix-9670s`.** Every other line on screen reads
box-drawing, then glyph, then who it is, and the fold marker is the header's
box-drawing — it holds that column and it says how the tree is shaped, not
how it is going. Putting the glyph after it leaves one order to read down the
whole screen and leaves the marker where a reader already looks for what is
folded. The marker did not move and `prefix()` was not touched. A tree whose
tracker never answered has no root to read, so it draws no glyph and says why
it failed instead.

**An elided run carries `✓`.** It said *closed* in words beside an empty
glyph column. `split` selects closed beads and nothing else, so the glyph is
the one state every member holds rather than a summary over mixed ones. Both
the glyph and its colour resolve through `row::status_glyph` and
`status_style`, so a run cannot drift from the beads it stands for, whatever
bdi-jxp makes closed.

**A line that stands for more than itself says how much of that is done.** A
leaf gets no count — it stands for itself alone and a fraction over one bead
only repeats its glyph. Everything else counts its whole subtree with its own
bead among the total, which is what a root's `35/51` already does
(`snapshot.rs` sets `total: nodes.len()`, and the root is one of those
nodes). Keyed on having children, never on `issue_type == "epic"`: reading
meaning out of a bd taxonomy field is interpreting a convention, and
conventions belong in config, whereas having children is the shape of the
tree bdi already computes and is exactly the condition that makes the
question askable. The count leads the state column, before the agent and the
warnings, in the order a header already puts them in.

**What a count does not cover, at either level.** A truncated node's
descendants were never in the tracker's answer, so a count above one covers
only what bd returned — in the fixtures `orb-7.1` reads `0/3` with
`orb-7.1.2` truncated beneath it. This is inherited, not introduced: a root's
count has always been over `nodes.len()`, and the tree's `Truncated` note is
what carries the honesty. The fraction degrades the same way at every depth
rather than a new way at one, and nothing tries to make it say more.

Wired behind the six remaining TUI beads (bdi-mse, bdi-xey, bdi-jxp, bdi-r5l, bdi-2bb.17, bdi-0mk) because its four original blockers all closed while the TUI was still being built. Its four deps were the beads that happened to be open when it was filed, not the set whose decisions it records — so bd ready called it spawnable, and a seat taking it would have written a design record that went stale within the hour. Each of the six changes something docs/design.md must state: the fold and run model, the default fold state, the status legend and its colours, the prefix layout, and the interaction bindings.

title: Three small corrections: a split constant, a dead field, two unused ones
description:
Three small corrections found in the 2026-08-30 architectural review. Each is
minutes; they are one bead because splitting them costs more than doing them.

**1. The tail's height is two constants that must agree, and nothing makes
them.** `src/view/draw.rs:628` has `const TAIL_LINES: u16 = 6;`, used at `:652`
to size the band. `src/view/tail.rs:17` has `pub const LINES: u16 = 6;`, used at
`src/tui.rs:570` and `:584` to say how many lines to ask herdr for. Change one
and the tail either scrolls off or leaves a blank row, and no test fails.
`draw.rs:626`'s comment states the relationship — in the file that does *not*
own the number `tui.rs` uses. Delete `draw::TAIL_LINES`; have `regions` use
`tail::LINES + 1`.

**2. `Line.last_child` is written seven times and read never.**
`src/view/forest.rs:48`, assigned at `:626`, `:674`, `:689`, `:725`, `:772`,
`:790` and `src/view/draw.rs:959`. `grep -rn last_child src/` returns exactly
those eight lines and no read. What it carries is already in the `prefix`
string, which `prefix()` (`:824`) builds from `last`. Delete the field and its
assignments.

**3. `Pane.workspace_id` and `Pane.tab_id` are parsed and never used.**
`src/collect/herdr.rs:33` and `:35`; their only other reference is a parse
assertion at `:158-159`. `docs/design.md` names them as the target for focus,
but `agent_focus` takes `pane_id`. YAGNI says delete. If they are kept, the
reason goes in the design, not in the struct.

## Done when

- One constant governs the tail's height, in the module whose meaning it is.
- `grep -rn last_child src/` returns nothing.
- Item 3 is either done or recorded here with the reason it was kept.

title: The (project, id) lookup is hand-rolled in four places
description:
**The key is `(project, id)`** — the cardinal rule of this codebase — is
implemented four separate times by hand, in two files.

| where | what it does |
|---|---|
| `src/view/forest.rs:531` `present` | `trees.any(project == && (root == id \|\| nodes.any(id)))` |
| `src/view/forest.rs:296` `live_under` | `trees.filter(project).find_map(nodes.position(id))` |
| `src/view/forest.rs:328` `ancestry` | `trees.filter(project)` … `nodes.position(id)` |
| `src/view/tail.rs:189` `agent` | `trees.filter(project).flat_map(nodes).find(id)` |

Each is correct today. Each is a place where the next person writes
`nodes.iter().find(|n| n.id == key.id)` without the project filter, and nothing
fails until two trackers collide — which `docs/design.md` treats as a matter of
time, not luck, because bead prefixes are per-tracker and uncoordinated.

**Two methods on `Snapshot` in `src/model/snapshot.rs`:**
`pub fn node(&self, key: &BeadKey) -> Option<&Node>` and
`pub fn holds(&self, key: &BeadKey) -> bool` — the second also matching a tree's
`root`, which `present` needs. All four call sites use them. The rule belongs
beside the type that carries both halves of the key.

## Done when

- No lookup by bead id outside `Snapshot` names `project` and `id` separately.
- The change deletes more lines than it adds.
- A test asserts that a bead id present in one project is not found through
  another project's key.
